en.title: Shortest, Then Smallest, String After Deleting Pairs of Equal Characters
en.description:
In each step you may delete any two equal characters, which need not be adjacent; the remaining characters keep their original order. First minimize the remaining length, then make the remaining string lexicographically smallest by Unicode code point.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The input is a JSON string. The original statement gives no upper bound on the length or the character domain; on this site 0≤length in code points≤200000, and all Unicode scalar characters are allowed, including whitespace, NUL, non-BMP characters and U+0085/U+2028/U+2029.
en.output: Output a canonical ASCII JSON string followed by a newline: double quotes and backslashes are escaped with a backslash; control characters use JSON short escapes (backspace, tab, newline, form feed, carriage return) or a lowercase four-digit \u; non-ASCII characters and DEL use a lowercase four-digit \u, and non-BMP characters use a pair of UTF-16 surrogate escapes; all other printable ASCII is output directly. This is equivalent to Python json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=True). An empty string is output as "". The exact comparison mode is used, so spaces inside the string cannot be ignored.
en.explanation: The outputs are "BAX", "XYZ" and "". The original third example shows a single space, which conflicts with its explicit explanation of an empty string; this site corrects it to an empty JSON string.
hints: Only characters with an odd frequency need to keep one copy each. Scan the original string and use the remaining frequencies, the set of chosen characters and a monotonic stack to pick the smallest subsequence that contains each of these characters exactly once.
